newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-SAMPDORIA AND INTER RE-OPEN TITLE CHASE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SAMPDORIA AND INTER RE-OPEN TITLE CHASE.

text.p: The playmaking skills of Sampdoria's Roberto Mancini and Internazionale's Youri Djorkaeff breathed new life into the Italian title race on Sunday, inspiring their sides to vital wins that narrowed Juventus's league lead to two points.

Veteran Mancini, tipped for a recall to Cesare Maldini's Italy side, made three goals in Sampdoria's impressive 4-1 win at home to Cagliari while Frenchman Djorkaeff made one and scored another in Inter's 2-1 win at Napoli.
The results took full advantage of Juventus's 0-0 draw at home to Atalanta, leaving Sampdoria and Inter level on 28 points from 16 matches although Sampdoria enjoy a superior goal difference.
The European champions, with two points in their last three matches, have seen a six-point New Year's advantage shrink rapidly.
Mancini, playing some of his best football since a move to Inter fell through, set Sampdoria on their way when he laid on Christian Karembeu's headed opener with a deep cross.
Cagliari levelled through Sandro Tovalieri in the 43rd minute only for Marco Carparelli to restore Sampdoria's lead four minutes into the second half.

Minutes later, the visitor's hopes of salvaging a point were left in ruins first by the dismissal of Daniel Berretta, then by the irrepressible Mancini, whose cross left Vincenzo Montella with a simple tap-in.

The unsettled Karembeu, caught in a bitter transfer tussle between Real Madrid and Barcelona, hardly improved his popularity at Sampdoria when he was sent-off for reacting to Luis Romero's late tackle in the 70th minute. The Uruguayan was also given his marching orders.
In injury-time, Mancini again set up Montella for his 10th goal in 10 appearances.
At Napoli, Djorkaeff's superb vision and touch wrested victory from defeat as Inter fought off continuous Napoli pressure to win with two opportunist goals.
First, the Frenchman set up Branca's snap shot in the 43rd minute that surprised goalkeeper Giuseppe Taglialatela.
Two minutes from time, Djorkaeff settled the issue by turning his marker and beating the hapless Taglialatela in one smooth movement.

Significantly, it was the third time in successive away matches that Inter have taken points from a game they might have lost and coach Roy Hodgson, who earlier this week accused Italian players of unsportsmanlike behaviour, admitted: "We were lucky."
To add to the visitor's good fortune, Napoli's Brazilian midfielder Beto was sent off for two deliberate handballs.
Napoli pulled a late goal back through Nicola Caccia.
Juventus were lucky to claim a point against Atalanta, as Gianluigi Lentini and Filippo Inzaghi both hit the woodwork in the second half.

To add to Juve's goalscoring problems, their main target-man Alen Boksic hobbled off midway through the first-half with a leg injury and will miss next Wednesday's European Supercup final first leg with Paris St.Germain in France.
Early season pacemakers Vicenza dropped to fourth on 26 points losing 1-0 to crisis-hit AC Milan.

Arrigo Sacchi left Dejan Savicevic and Roberto Baggio on the bench, preferring to play Christophe Dugarry as a lone striker. In the 19th minute, the Frenchman repaid his manager by heading home Marco Simone's cross.
After the break, the champions lost midfielder Marcel Desailly to his second bookable offence and were forced to fight a rearguard action for their first win in three matches.
In the 88th and 90th minutes, Roberto Murgita and Maurizio Rossi twice had the ball in the Milan net but both goals were disallowed for off-side.
Milan now lie sixth on 24 points, level with Parma, who followed-up successive wins over Arrigo Sacchi's side and Juventus with a 1-0 win at Bologna.
Parma's old manager Nevio Scala made a disastrous debut on the Perugia bench, watching his new side crash 4-1 to Roma.
